chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah is Gentle (Rafiq); He grants the reward and He loves every gentle person, and He grants for gentleness that which He does not grant for harshness.'

key_terms.الرِّفْقُ: Gentleness, ease, or mildness in conduct.
key_terms.الْعُنْفُ: Harshness, force, or severity in conduct.
key_terms.رَفِيقٌ: Gentle, kind, or mild; a divine attribute denoting Allah's gentleness.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of gentleness (Rifq) in Islamic ethics according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Jabir al-Ju'fi to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), underscores 'Rifq' as a divine attribute that Allah not only embodies but also loves in His creation. It establishes a theological principle that gentleness yields unique, superior rewards distinct from those of harshness, a concept central to Shia ethical teachings on character refinement. The narration serves as a practical guide for believers to emulate divine gentleness in their interactions, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of mercy.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 12.ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “

The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Verily Allah is kind, He grants [abundant] reward [to the virtuous] and He loves every kind [and gentle] person. He grants for gentleness that which He does not grant for [anything which involves] harshness.’”[1]
